note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent judge, authored none of spec-rfc4301-architecture-gaps). Section 4.1: "The receiver MUST process the packets from the different SAs without prejudice." The stale unit TestRFC4301BoundarySADEntryIsRefusedRatherThanInstalledWrong changed only its RFC4301-4.1-9 negative claim, from "no second SA is ever shadowed by a malformed one", wider than any assertion, to "an SA whose mode or integrity transform the kernel cannot hold is refused and no SAD entry is built for it"; the body is unchanged and asserts exactly that for mode 9 and an unknown integrity transform (error and nil state). The reworded claim owes a fresh discrimination record. The stack proof stays the positive TestRFC4301ParallelSAsWithOneSelectorAreEachReceived; the negatives stay supplementary, as judged before. Verdict stands. Prior judgement: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after c85342c940). Section 4.1: "The receiver MUST process the packets from the different SAs without prejudice." The two dataplane SAD boundary units changed only by the deleted RFC4301-4.4.2.1-3 tag lines; their bodies are identical, and the engine units are byte-identical. Judged on the positive under owner ruling 5: TestRFC4301ParallelSAsWithOneSelectorAreEachReceived installs two Child SAs on one selector pair through createFirstChildSA over real XFRM in a rootless netns and delivers an in-selector packet on SA1, SA2, then SA1 again; a per-SA template or reqid mismatch, or shared replay state that dropped the sibling's packets, goes red. The builder positive asserts two SAD entries with distinct SPIs 0x1000 and 0x2000 from xfrmStateFromParams. The negatives (TestRFC4301ParallelSAsAreHeldToTheOneSharedPolicy, which proves the 4.4.1-10 post-decryption SPD check, and the SAD refusal unit, which proves an unbuildable SA installs nothing) stay supplementary: no receive-side input can inject prejudiced processing.
